Replay

Replay canonical schema and message codecs

7 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
ContractsPublic and authority projectionsEnvelopesVerificationField differencesCompiled validationSparse validation blocksStructural compression metadataLocal scalar authoring

Use replay/schema to encode portable values for packets, archives and diagnostics. It builds a bounded scalar-field program from Odin compiler type information and encodes logical values independently of struct padding, native offsets and endian-qualified scalar storage. No scriptgen attributes are required.

Initialization also compiles validation indices and contiguous copy spans. The codec still validates constrained values before writing; adjacent canonical bytes then copy in bulk. Padding, excluded fields and endian-qualified values split spans as needed. This local program does not change fingerprints or wire bytes. Schema options are fixed at initialization; rebuild a schema to change them.

Odin
State :: struct {
    position: [2]f32,
    health: i32,
    director_seed: u64 `replay:"authority"`,
}

schema: sc.Schema
report := sc.init(&schema, State)
defer sc.destroy(&schema) // also required after a failed initialization

// Callers own their buffers. encode/decode do not allocate.
report = sc.encode(&schema, state, bytes[:])
report = sc.decode(&schema, &candidate, bytes[:schema.wire_size])

Contracts#

  • Scalars have fixed wire widths and little-endian encoding. Packed and padded structs with identical logical fields produce identical fingerprints/bytes.
  • Fixed-width integers, f16/f32/f64, one-byte booleans, enums, bit sets, fixed arrays, enumerated arrays, ordinary nested structs and value-safe tagged unions are supported. See the tagged-union contract.
  • Pointer-bearing/dynamic types, raw unions, platform-width serialized integers, unsupported widths, and unknown replay tags are rejected with a field path. An enum used only to index an array or bit set does not itself cross the wire, so its semantic names/values are recorded without imposing a serialized width.
  • Finite floats are required by default; booleans, enum values, and bit-set masks are validated. Ordinary integer ranges and cross-field/game rules remain the admission layer's responsibility. Unused fixed-storage enum fields must still have a legal value; include an explicit zero member when zero initialization is used.
  • Decode requires exact payload length and commits only after complete validation. Encode preflights values before writing any destination byte.
  • Schemas own metadata/path strings and retain compiler-owned enum metadata. They must not outlive their compiled module. Do not copy live schema owners.
  • Limits bound recursive depth, paths, logical field count, canonical metadata, and wire bytes. This is a fixed-value format; large assets need chunking and managed dynamic collections need a separate storage/codec contract.

Schema.canonical is the readable compatibility description. The fingerprint includes projection, float policy, field names/order, widths, array/index meaning, enum definitions, and authority annotations. It excludes native offsets, padding, type aliases, and the native/endian-qualified representation of equivalent scalars. Changing gameplay code/assets also requires a content/semantic version; a schema fingerprint alone cannot detect changes to game rules.

Public and authority projections#

DEFAULT_OPTIONS describes a complete authority value. To construct a public projection, copy those options and set projection = .Public. Fields under replay:"authority" are omitted from its payload. Public decode preserves those excluded fields in the supplied destination value. The entire declared type is still checked for portable checkpoint compatibility.

The public projection and full authority checkpoint have different fingerprints. The session uses the public projection for ordinary snapshots and the full projection for authority checkpoints and authorized recovery holders. A filtered public value is not sufficient to resume an authority, nor automatically sufficient to predict gameplay that depends on excluded state.

Envelopes#

pack and unpack add a 52-byte versioned envelope around one canonical value:

Text
magic[4], version:u16, kind:u16, epoch:u64, tick:u64,
schema:u64, content:u64, body_bytes:u32, checksum:u64, body

The wire magic is RPLY; version is currently 1. Envelope_Meta supplies message kind, authority epoch, tick, and content contract. unpack requires matching kind/epoch/content and schema, checks exact length and checksum, then decodes transactionally. Its returned tick still needs the session's timing validation; expected.tick is intentionally unused.

inspect only reads untrusted routing metadata. It is not a substitute for unpack or for checking transport sender identity. FNV fingerprints/checksums detect compatibility changes and accidental corruption; they are not signatures, authentication, or encryption. Envelopes supply framing; durable-save versioning and host migration require their separate archive and authority protocols.

Verification#

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_schema/run.sh

Native tests pin bytes, padding/endian equivalence, projections, enum/bit-set validation, field diagnostics, transactional failure, allocation ownership, and envelope mutation/truncation rejection. The gate also type-checks the instantiated schema/correction/transport/adapter surface for WASM. That type-check alone does not establish cross-platform replay or execution parity; see the separate tagged-union execution evidence for its tested corpus.

Field differences#

diff(schema, left, right, output) and diff_encoded(schema, left_payload, right_payload, output) compare canonical fields using the same validation and projection as the codec. They validate both complete inputs before writing any output, return a total count independently of display capacity and allocate nothing. Differences carry borrowed field paths and canonical scalar bits. diff_value returns owned readable text, including enum names and exact integer values. See audit captures and diagnostics for equality rules, metadata lifetimes and an example that connects a local audit failure to field paths.

Compiled validation#

Flat schemas compile a compact validation program alongside their copy spans. The hot loop reads offsets, widths and validation rules directly, without copying full diagnostic field descriptors. Boolean and finite-float checks retain their existing rules. Bit sets use their declared mask; small enums use exact bit sets, ascending ranges use bounds, and sparse/wide enums retain exact membership checks. Native qualified-endian and packed/unaligned fields still use byte-safe reads.

The program preserves field order and returns the same first invalid field path. Validation completes before encoding writes output or decoding commits a candidate. Tagged unions retain the general guard-aware validator. Only local compiled metadata changes: canonical fields, fingerprints, envelope checksums and bytes do not. No runtime code generation, platform-specific vector instruction or relaxed float validation is introduced. Schema owns and releases the program with its other metadata; do not mutate compiled schema metadata after initialization.

The codec benchmark compares exact bytes and timing with an explicitly retained reference implementation. Use game-level profiles and workload comparisons to assess the practical benefit.

The FNV-1a compatibility digest keeps its exact historical bytes/seed behavior. Its scan recognizes bounded eight-byte zero blocks and applies prime^8 modulo 2^64; dense blocks and tails retain the ordered byte fold. Loads are explicitly unaligned, and the zero test is endian-independent. This changes scan cost, not fingerprints, envelope validation or cryptographic guarantees.

Sparse validation blocks#

For non-union schemas, initialization also groups zero-valid checks within one existing direct-copy span, up to 32 checks and 128 bytes per block. A wholly zero block is valid without interpreting each scalar. Booleans, finite floats and bit sets accept zero; an enum must explicitly contain zero. Nonzero-only enums keep their normal check. No scan crosses padding, omitted private fields, reversed scalar storage or guarded union storage.

A bounded per-call probe samples up to eight compiled blocks. Two zero blocks select grouped validation; otherwise the original scalar loop handles the value. The decision is not cached and changes no schema state, so dense and sparse values can alternate safely. Nonzero blocks fall back in original field order, preserving first-error paths. Encode/decode still validate fully before writing output.

This adds local metadata and retains a small dense-input overhead in the measured microbenchmark. It changes no canonical bytes, fingerprints, public projection or wire/save version. Oracle checks and measurement evidence record the supported cases and tradeoffs.

Structural compression metadata#

Schema initialization also records disjoint outer array regions in canonical byte coordinates. Version 1 selects fixed arrays with at least four elements, at least 256 public/authority wire bytes as appropriate, and element width greater than one. An eligible outer array replaces nested candidates. Variant-specific arrays inside union payloads are excluded because their storage can overlap; a fixed array of whole tagged unions can still be transformed as fixed-width records.

shuffle(schema, canonical, grouped) places equal byte positions from successive array elements together. unshuffle reverses that permutation exactly. Bytes outside the selected regions retain their positions. Both require disjoint, exact-size buffers and leave the destination unchanged on rejected arguments. They operate on serialized bytes, so padding, private-field projection and native endianness do not leak into the transform.

Schema.shuffle_fingerprint identifies the transform version, canonical schema, wire size and ordered regions. It is separate from the canonical fingerprint. Changing the wire transform requires a new transform contract; receivers must not infer a different permutation from a matching ordinary schema alone. These helpers are compression primitives: canonical bytes and ordinary encode/decode stay exact.

Local scalar authoring#

field_index(&schema, "$.path") resolves a scalar leaf. scalar_text(&schema, value, index) returns owned display text and an Edit_Error; free successful text with delete. edit_scalar(&schema, &value, index, text, validator) validates and commits one scalar change transactionally. Pass a typed proc(State)->bool for application invariants, or nil when schema checks suffice. The helper requires an authority projection, rejects inactive leaves and union-tag changes, and preserves the destination on any failure. Integer parsing checks overflow before arithmetic; float narrowing rejects overflow and nonfinite values. It supports packed/endian-qualified values through canonical bytes, without a wire-format change. See the Godot preview editor.
